subject: BridgePath access onboarding: SSO / SCIM / IP gating — sequencing & kickoff
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@bridgepath.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: BridgePath access onboarding — SSO / SCIM / IP gating

Hi Liam,

Thanks for choosing Redwood — excited to partner on BridgePath's enterprise rollout.
Per our pre-sales notes, we want to align on sequence and responsibilities for SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning, IP allowlists, and the service account model.

Proposed high-level sequence (we can adjust on the call):
- Day 0: kickoff + collect SAML metadata and IP ranges
- Week 1: SAML integration (test IdP → Redwood staging)
- Week 2: SCIM provisioning pilot with 5 test users using svc account
- Week 3: IP allowlist cutover and staging verification
- Week 4: Rollout + monitoring + org policy checks

Pre-kickoff asks (please attach or send before our call):
- SAML metadata (entityID, ACS URL, cert) — filename convention accepted
- SCIM admin account (or service account) details and expected user attributes
- IP ranges for allowlisting (CIDR blocks) and any proxy/egress notes
- SOC2 or security contact for questionnaire and cert expiry dates

I attached an initial access checklist to guide the call. Suggested slots: Tue/Thu this week — what works for you?

Best,
— Olga
Olga Petrov
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi team,
Couple of internal notes / proposal from Redwood infra side:
- Keep SAML cutover isolated: verify test users in staging before any production assertion flows.
- SCIM: use a dedicated service account with token rotation policy; restrict to user.read/write for the pilot group only.
- IP allowlist: we recommend a maintenance window for adding CIDRs and validating egress; include rollback steps in case of blocked integrations.
- Org policies: confirm whether BridgePath enforces device posture or conditional access; those may require additional header/certificate exchange.

I'll draft an implementation plan and attach it here for the call so we have a concrete checklist.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
